c1-09-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Hospital Should Have Done
c1-09-01.scenario: You and a friend talk about a news story: a hospital did not tell a patient's relatives in time.
c1-09-01.prompt: Say that telling the relatives was the hospital's duty, and that the harm would have been avoidable.
cues: Say what would have been avoided
c1-09-01.target: A kórháznak kötelessége lett volna azonnal értesíteni a hozzátartozókat. Ha időben értesítették volna őket, a baj elkerülhető lett volna.
c1-09-01.english: It would have been the hospital's duty to notify the relatives at once. If they had been notified in time, the harm would have been avoidable.
c1-09-01.canDo: I can say that a harm would have been avoidable if someone had acted (*Ha … volna, elkerülhető lett volna …*).

c1-09-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Likely, but Not Enough
c1-09-02.scenario: A friend says that an operation will surely succeed, so the patient's consent hardly matters.
c1-09-02.prompt: Answer that the operation will probably succeed, but informed consent is still a duty.
cues: Say how likely the success is
Say what is still a duty
c1-09-02.target: A kezelés minden bizonnyal sikeres lesz, de a tájékozott beleegyezés akkor is etikai kötelesség.
c1-09-02.english: The treatment will almost certainly succeed, but informed consent is still an ethical duty.
c1-09-02.canDo: I can tell what is likely from what is a duty (*minden bizonnyal sikeres*, *etikai kötelesség*).

c1-09-03.title: Communicative Challenge: One Free Bed
c1-09-03.scenario: You and a friend talk about a hospital with one free bed and two patients.
c1-09-03.prompt: Say that whichever patient the doctor chooses, the other loses a chance.
c1-09-03.target: Bármelyik beteget választja is az orvos, a másik elveszíti az esélyét. Ez nagy lelkiismereti konfliktus.
c1-09-03.english: Whichever patient the doctor chooses, the other loses his chance. This is a serious conflict of conscience.
c1-09-03.canDo: I can describe a hard choice where every decision has a moral cost (*két rossz közül a kisebbik*).

c1-09-04.title: Communicative Challenge: What a Patient May Refuse
c1-09-04.scenario: A friend asks what an incurably ill patient may refuse by law.
c1-09-04.prompt: Say that under strict conditions the patient may refuse life-sustaining treatment, and say what a living will is.
cues: Say what the patient has the right to refuse
Say what a living will does
c1-09-04.target: Szigorú feltételek mellett a betegnek joga van visszautasítani az életfenntartó kezelést. Az élő végrendeletben előre leírhatja az akaratát.
c1-09-04.english: Under strict conditions the patient has the right to refuse life-sustaining treatment. In a living will he can write down his wishes in advance.
c1-09-04.canDo: I can say what a patient may refuse and decide (*önrendelkezési jog*, *az életfenntartó kezelés visszautasítása*).

c1-09-05.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Text Says About the Doctor
c1-09-05.scenario: You have read a short text about László Németh, a writer who also worked as a physician, and a friend asks what it says about the doctor's work.
c1-09-05.prompt: Tell your friend what the text says the doctor must not become and what the doctor should do.
cues: Say what the doctor must not become
Say what the doctor should do instead
c1-09-05.target: A szöveg szerint az orvos nem lehet puszta szerelő. Az egész embert kell gyógyítania.
c1-09-05.english: According to the text, the doctor cannot be a mere mechanic. He has to treat the whole person.
c1-09-05.canDo: I can report what a text says about a writer's ideas (*A szöveg szerint …*).

c1-09-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Likely, but the Patient Decides
c1-09-consolidation.scenario: A friend asks what you remember from this unit about a treatment and the patient.
c1-09-consolidation.prompt: Say that the treatment will probably help, but the patient decides and the doctor must inform him.
cues: Say how likely the help is
Say what the doctor must do
c1-09-consolidation.target: A kezelés feltehetőleg segít, de a döntés a betegé. Az orvosnak kötelessége szólni neki.
c1-09-consolidation.english: The treatment will presumably help, but the decision is the patient's. It is the doctor's duty to inform him.
c1-09-consolidation.canDo: I can look back on a harm and say what would have been avoidable.
